name: Logto
description: Logto is an open-source identity and access management platform. It acts as an OpenID Connect, OAuth 2.1 and SAML provider with a hosted sign-in experience, social and enterprise SSO, MFA, role-based access control, organizations for multi-tenant apps and a Management API, all administered through a web Admin Console. This script installs it with a local PostgreSQL database.

notes.text: There is no default account. Open the Admin Console at https://<IP>:3002 and choose Create account. The open-source edition allows exactly one admin account, and anyone who reaches port 3002 can create it until you do, so do it right after the install.

Both ports use a self-signed certificate, because the Admin Console only works in a secure context. Accept it on https://<IP>:3001 as well as on https://<IP>:3002, since the console calls the API on port 3001. The certificate is valid for 365 days.

ENDPOINT (port 3001, sign-in and OIDC issuer at /oidc) and ADMIN_ENDPOINT (port 3002, Admin Console) in /opt/logto_data/.env must match the URLs that browsers and apps use. For real OIDC use, put Logto behind a reverse proxy with a trusted certificate: set both to your HTTPS domains, add TRUST_PROXY_HEADER=1, remove HTTPS_CERT_PATH and HTTPS_KEY_PATH, then run systemctl restart logto.
